\begin{figure}[!tbp]
  \centering
  \includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{../figures/out/rse_fig_gsl.pdf}
  \caption{\textbf{The same audit at Great Salt Lake, Utah, with a lake-bed control from echo soundings.}
  (a, b)~For each arm, the shoreline displacement $D$ at each level bin (NAVD~88), after each surface's area-fitted offset, against the observation noise floor $Q$ (grey area; Fig.~\ref{fig:rse_method}c).
  Coloured lines: the five global grids; open markers on the top edge, levels where a grid predicts no shoreline.
  Grey dashed line: the 3DEP control, mostly 2016 lidar.
  Black line: the lake-bed control (USGS echo soundings below the sounded top, map contours and the National Elevation Dataset above it); filled where $D > Q$.
  Shaded columns: the sounded levels.
  (c)~For each arm and surface, the median $D$ over the evaluable levels (marker) against the median $Q$ (grey bar ending in a tick); filled where it fails the shoreline test ($D > Q$ at more than half of the levels).
  The lake-bed control is shown over all its levels (\metric{rev2.g.lakebed.all.north.shape.n_evaluable} north, \metric{rev2.g.lakebed.all.south.shape.n_evaluable} south) and over the sounded levels alone, with its offset refitted on them; there it fails both arms (\metric{rev2.g.lakebed.sounded.north.shape.n_exceeding} of \metric{rev2.g.lakebed.sounded.north.shape.n_evaluable} and \metric{rev2.g.lakebed.sounded.south.shape.n_exceeding} of \metric{rev2.g.lakebed.sounded.south.shape.n_evaluable} levels).
  Logarithmic axes.
  (d)~Heights of each grid over each arm's emerged band (share of cells per half-metre bin); dotted line, the gauge level of February 2000, when SRTM flew.}
  \label{fig:rse_gsl}
\end{figure}
